correctness.rationale: Direct monotonicity on the nonnegative-height positive-speed quadrant and open trapping/ballistic inequalities establish the three regimes and at least one critical interval for every lambda,y0. On any critical orbit exact telescoping velocity losses plus a summable, explicitly controlled left-Riemann excess yield u=lambda/y+lambda(lambda-1)/(3y^3)+O(y^-5). Then the squared-height increment is 2lambda+lambda(5lambda-2)/(3y²)+O(y^-4), so subtracting 2lambda*n+(5lambda-2)/6 log(n) leaves a convergent sum. The independent symbolic coefficient identity and finite critical shooting diagnostics are reproducible from verify.py; finite tests do not substitute for the infinity proof.

value.rationale: The model has a continuum of equilibria, so fixed-point eigenvalues alone do not classify how trajectories either settle or escape. The theorem identifies an unavoidable parabolic boundary between both open basins for every height and every 0<lambda<1, gives an exact all-critical-orbit square-root law, and detects a nontrivial second-order sign reversal at lambda=2/5. This supplies quantitative global boundary geometry and escape clocks beyond the source numerical phase portraits, without needing a paper-sized downstream application.
